interactions.title: Rai explains his failed ritual and Apollyon’s prison
lines: DM: Yeah. All right. Okay. So you rest, um, recover. Um, Rai is not super talkative. It seems like, uh, it takes a fair bit of effort to just maintain everything that he's trying to maintain. But you do, I mean, you do hear a little bit more about the, you know, everything that happened and how most of the story of the events leading up to Rai getting caught here, you've pretty much figured out by now, I think.

DM: But basically he met some of the monks. He got worried that the wound was getting worse, and came up here, talked to Beryl, hashed a strategy, and didn't realize until they got to Isingue with all the monks and started doing this ritual to close a portal that it wasn't in fact a portal, and got ripped through. Managed to save most of the monks, but it has taken pretty much all of his...

DM: Oh, and as he g— he tells you as he got, as he was getting ripped through, he knew there was gonna be trouble, and he just sent out a desperate message to the only person he was telepathically connected to at the time, Dimitaur: "Please go find some powerful Dunmari, tell them what happened, bring help."
Kenzo: Dimitaur did not do that.
DM: Dimitaur didn't, did not do that. [laughs]
DM: He probably, like, went to go look for the Dunmari and saw one of the dragonets who were coming from the circular island, and was like, "What's this?" And followed them back.
DM: 'Cause you know he only showed up on the circular island after Rai vanished, right?
Kenzo: But then, but then, um, Rai was also in Drankor. Like, what was Rai doing with Apollyon? Because he was doing something with Apollyon, too.
DM: Well, he originally teleported to Drankor after Cha'mutte died to stop—
DM: ... Apollyon from summoning his phylactery.
DM: Which would've cut through Cha'mutte's prison and released Apollyon into the world.
DM: But he basically re— he basically reinforced Cha'mutte's prison and hid the phylac... Remember you spent—
DM: ... forever, like he reinforced Cha'mutte's prison and hid the phylactery, and then he was sort of like, "Well, what else do I have to do?"
DM: That's why he started talking to the monks and trying to go back to his original goal, which was to finish the Great War and deal with Cha'mutte's issues.
Kenzo: Cleaning up. The cleaning up thing.
DM: Cleaning up, yeah. Apollyon was pretty stable, and would've... I, I mean, nothing would've happened except that.
Kenzo: So Apollyon destabilizing and starting to escape, and then Rai ending up in the Ooze dimension, or in Limbo?

DM: What hap... A— Apollyon, Apollyon was only able to dis— destabilize and start to escape because he was talking to... He had corrupted the whole Cleansed and had gotten Fausto to do all this work to get the ritual to go off that... Right? That was our whole—
Kenzo: And then ultimately if Rai, Rai had been around, he might have, like, been able to intervene or, you know, do something.
Unknown: But he was not around.
DM: Yeah, he might've been able to.
Kenzo: So that original vision where, like, Rai's hand explo— Like the, that, that vision that we kept seeing over and over again, that was...
DM: That was the moment that he tried to close the portal.
DM: And his hand exploded in part because of the way he... You know, because the magic was... He was using the wrong magic.

before: DM: But you don't, it doesn't give you that much benefit in terms of the flight or the pass through objects.
Unknown: Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm.

DM: Yeah. Um, you can change, uh, you can change Aura Focus as a bonus action, but you can also use Flurry of Blows as part of the same bonus action.
Kenzo: That's... Okay. So you can, I can basically move Aura Focus around on our own.
after: Kenzo: Have you known that Rai was in Limbo this whole, this whole campaign?
DM: Yeah. Well, so to be fair, I didn't... I knew that Rai... I, I basically knew what happened, but the whole Limbo-Isingue connection actually—
Unknown: Yeah.
DM: ... grew out of you—
Unknown: Flying over.

lines: DM: Yeah, let's wait. Okay. Like, they've lost people who fell off, who like got distracted and weren't focused on the task, and so drifted out, slowly decaying more and more.

DM: And at least a few of them were just have been completely lost to Limbo itself. So they try, you know, they're pretty, uh, rigorous about making sure that they stick to their routines and their, um, uh, and their patterns.

interactions.title: Rai’s advice about the entity and the relic
lines: Kenzo: So, you know, obviously we've never fought, uh, original Limbo beings, um—
Kenzo: ... that we know of. Um, so any advice if, when, if when we encounter them? Helpful, helpful tips?
DM: He thinks for a minute. [clears throat]
Seeker: Vulnerabilities, sensitive topics, discuss with them.
DM: All, all I can sense from a distance wrestling with her—
DM: ... is that, um, she has an incredible force of will.
Seeker: Which is exactly what makes you strong and stable here in Limbo.
Unknown: Is that— One of us has a force of will.
Seeker: ... a little bit metagame, correspond to Constitution?
Delwath: No, it's probably mental saves. It probably has like almost un... Probably spells that require save, mental saves, would be very difficult/pointless.
DM: Yeah. So target dex or strength or maybe con. Don't attempt—don't waste your spells on the plus 15 wisdom, charisma, and intelligence saves—
DM: ... is the advice Rai is giving you.
Kenzo: We'll ask him about the Order of Stability.
Seeker: Big or small? We'll, we'll find out.
DM: He's only, like, struggled with—like, mentally wrestled for control of the relic with her. He hasn't ever seen her.

DM: ... covered in runes that you have, that lets you move the—

Kenzo: Otherwise, it's time for you to dissolve into Limbo and chaos.

interactions.title: Otesea and Elbos admit the visitors
lines: DM: ... meanwhile, the two stone creatures—
DM: ... clank, clank over towards you.

DM: As they move. There's like, the smoke is, like, hardening into metal, and it's like, as they move, there's like metal plates clanking. They look, and one of them says, rapidly cycling through languages, each word a different language, but Kenzo can understand all languages.
DM: So you understand. "Visitors. Visitors. Strange." Looks over at his or her companion. "Are you here to worship? Have you come to give yourselves to the Great Goal?"
Unknown: The Great what? Goal. Goal. Like G-O-A-L?
Seeker: Uh, yes. We're here to worship.
DM: ... in front of the door, uh, Otesea did say—
DM: ... "Don't," the other one, Elbos, "don't... We don't know who these are. Don't tell them anything."

DM: "We're guests. We're here." Um, and they're like, "Maybe they are, um... Okay, well at least you came to the front door."
DM: "Um, we'll let you in." The moment they say that the door swings open and you see Wellby—

DM: [laughs] Uh, do you want to do anything with your action? And their, their look of their face like, "Do you know these intruders?"

DM: "That... We, um, no. It's in— imperative. I, I must tell... Uh, yeah, no. Um."

DM: "Go, go, go ahead and wait in the antechamber and when it's safe—"
Wellby: Can we communicate with them telepathically?
Unknown: Yeah, we can tell them what's going on.
DM: No, now we're all inside. Yeah, yeah. You, you actually—
DM: Um, hold on. Let me—
DM: ... let me do things in order. Um, so, so they step in. They're like shooing, shooing the—

DM: "Um, with lots of spikes that seem to be made out of glass or water, water spikes. They look very sharp."

interactions.title: Named warriors in the statue hall
lines: DM: Um, it's very, it happens quietly. Um, you see, like, a d— um, a dozen statues of strange warriors similar to, like, the humanoids in the, um, in the m— mosaic below. They're like... You wouldn't even really describe them as humanoids, but they're clearly warriors. There's about a dozen of these statues, each surrounded by a semicircle of, I guess what you might describe as candles, but each one seems to be made of some weird different material. Like, there's one of stone, there's one that's made of water that's just a pillar of water, and all the candles are, are burning. It's almost like a... They're almost like... It's like in a church. It's like the sort of tealights in front of an altar in a church.

DM: Um, there are four pedestals that are much larger than the rest. Um, three hold big statues. One is a statue of whirlwind made of white stone forming a vaguely humanoid shape while the inside of the whirlwind dances with crystals of frost. Um, and it has a, a script that's labeled, and again, it seems like every language at once, and it says, "Pel Ossa, the Chalk Storm."

DM: Another looks like raindrops rising from the ground, each bursting into a fireball as they ascend, forming a humanoid torso that floats on a cloud of wh— ... flaming dust water. That says, "Zalmira, the Arid Rain."
